mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has reversed from -12.9% (t-3w) to +1.7% (t-0w), signaling restored outdoor leisure activity. This reversal will sustain and drive complementary retail-and-recreation visits as consumers redirect discretionary spending toward in-person retail experiences co-located with parks and recreation zones over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 14.6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below or declines relative to the prior 28-day mean despite PARKS maintaining positive or near-zero values.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has increased to +11.7% at t-0w, indicating heightened home-based activity and reduced commuting. This sustained elevation in residential presence suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility as consumers substitute in-home leisure and e-commerce for physical retail visits, producing lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at +11.7% at t-0w, highest in snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases relative to the prior 28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above +10%.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility has collapsed to -14.0% at t-0w, the lowest point in the snapshot. When transit falls below -13%, commuting infrastructure stress and reduced foot traffic through transit-adjacent retail zones trigger a cascading decline in retail-and-recreation mobility that persists for two weeks before stabilizing.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days increases relative to the prior 14-day mean despite TRANSIT remaining below -13%.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility has stabilized at -3.6% (t-0w), indicating essential-goods purchasing is normalized. When grocery-and-pharmacy stabilizes near baseline while parks recover, consumers reallocate discretionary spending from essential to non-essential retail, driving retail-and-recreation upward over the next four weeks through a substitution effect.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM within -5% to 0% AND PARKS above -5%
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM converging to baseline while PARKS recovered
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days declines or remains flat relative to the prior 28-day mean when both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS meet the trigger condition.

When workplace mobility falls more than 8 percentage points week-on-week, retail-and-recreation follows with a one-week lag as office-based discretionary spending evaporates.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week decline exceeds 8 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -4.4% to -13.1% in one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days increases relative to the prior 7-day mean following a >8 percentage point WORKPLACES decline.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility at +11.7% combined with transit collapse at -14.0% indicates a regime shift toward remote work and reduced commuting. This dual signal—high residential, low transit—suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility because consumers lack the commute-time opportunity to visit retail zones, producing lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days increases relative to the prior 14-day mean when both RESIDENTIAL and TRANSIT meet the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has recovered to +1.7% at t-0w after sustained negative values. This recovery, combined with grocery-and-pharmacy stabilization at -3.6%, signals consumer confidence in outdoor and essential activities. This confidence will extend to retail-and-recreation visits within one week as consumers resume discretionary shopping alongside parks and grocery trips.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days declines relative to the prior 7-day mean when PARKS is positive and GROCERY_PHARM is above -5%.

mechanism_narrative: Retail-and-recreation has shown a consistent upward trend from -10.0% (t-3w) to -5.6% (t-0w), a 4.4-point improvement over three weeks. This monotonic recovery signal indicates underlying demand restoration. Absent a shock to transit or workplaces, this trend will continue, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as the recovery momentum persists.
